text: Always look people in the face when you speak to them: the not doing it is thought to imply conscious guilt; besides that you lose the advantage of serving by their countenances what impression your discourse makes upon them. In order to know people's real sentiments, I trust much more to my eyes than to my ears: for they can say whatever they have a mind I should hear; but they can seldom help looking, what they have no intention that I should know.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter LIV, to his son, Bath, October 19, Old Style 1748
